response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(1.0 * w / NULLIF(g, 0)) AS avg_win_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id) SELECT team_id, avg_win_rate, record_count, avg_win_rate - (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) FROM t) AS diff_from_mean FROM t ORDER BY (avg_win_rate - (SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) FROM t)) IS NULL, diff_from_mean DESC, team_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Teams are grouped by team_id alone, so a team's records are pooled across years and leagues.
A record with g = 0 or NULL g or w has no win rate. It is left out of the average but still counted in record_count.
The mean of all team averages is an unweighted average of the per-team averages, skipping teams whose average is NULL.
Ties in the difference are broken by team_id, which the request does not specify.
